reason: Proves an event was drained; the properties (policy_denied event with fixed action, resource and detail, and no request bytes) are asserted in the loop at lines 1532-1543, and saw_denial at line 1544 is the loop floor.

test_name: request deadline arms and clears
broken_impl: armRequestDeadline sets deadline_ns to a tiny constant such as 1 (already expired) and the test passes
reason: armRequestDeadlineMs sets deadline_ns = now + ms*1e6 with a 50 ms timeout, so it must be at least the time read before the call plus 50 ms.
proposed_assertion: const before = compat.monotonicNowNs(); arm; expect(rt.ctx.deadline_ns >= before + 50 * std.time.ns_per_ms)

test_name: every row names its parameters and a next action that is not a guess
broken_impl: a row with a single-space or placeholder description passes
reason: Description is free prose published by meta. A golden would be brittle, a structural property (pairwise distinct) does not refuse a single placeholder, and no execution result applies. Non-empty is the stable contract.

test_name: every row names its parameters and a next action that is not a guess
broken_impl: none; a row with no parameters cannot contain a refusal. entry
reason: names_refusal at line 156 needs at least one parameter starting with refusal., so the length check is implied. Line 156 is not a weak assertion.

test_name: the real counter measures every scratch case with a nonzero cost
broken_impl: counter returns a constant 1 per case; instruction counts are hardware dependent
reason: Exact instruction counts are not part of the contract. Structural: costs.len==4 is asserted at line 1369. Growth with work is asserted by the instruction_counter test at instruction_counter.zig:275. No stable golden exists.

test_name: simulate flags newly introduced canonical diagnostics
broken_impl: new_count counts the wrong set of violations (for example all violations) and the test passes
reason: new_count is incremented once per violation with introduced_by_patch (edit_simulate.zig line 190-192).
proposed_assertion: count violations where v.introduced_by_patch inside the loop and expectEqual(@as(u32, thatCount), result.new_count)

test_name: compute fills all fields
broken_impl: rule_count is wrong but consistent with category sums (for example both 1)
reason: rule_count is policy_catalog.rules().len in compute(); the categories sum is pinned to it at line 137, but neither is tied to the registry.

test_name: the committed census clears its floors and every expectation states a reason
broken_impl: a probe with reason " " passes; reason text is free prose
reason: Reason strings are free prose. Tried: structural (distinct reasons, but identical reasons are legitimate for sibling probes), execution (not applicable), golden (brittle). Non-empty is the stable contract of the test name.

test_name: the generator yields unique names and renders every placeholder
broken_impl: a probe with reason " " passes; reason text is free prose
reason: Reason strings are free prose with legitimate repeats across the matrix. No structural property or golden is stable. Line 1304 is the placeholder-rendering check.

test_name: counter names its source and never silently falls back on macOS
broken_impl: counter always returns 1 (non-zero constant) and the test passes
reason: Absolute reading is process dependent. The stronger property (reading grows with work and doubles within a window) is asserted by the next test at instruction_counter.zig:275.

test_name: counter cost grows with the work done
broken_impl: none; the ratio check at line 275 divides by small and fails when it is 0 on counting sources
reason: small>0 guards the division. The ratio window 1.5..2.5 at line 275 pins growth on instruction-counting sources. Non-counting fallback sources rely on this line alone.

test_name: pipeline mutation: the check holds its contract on mutated corpus and examples
broken_impl: the run produces no diagnostic at all, so position and determinism checks see no diagnostic
reason: Floor on the diagnostics reached; the properties (no diagnostic outside the mutant, deterministic replays, zero failures) are asserted by checkMutant and line 501.

test_name: pipeline regression: a guarded verifyWebhookSignature call keeps fault_covered
broken_impl: fault_total is wrong or zero because the call is invisible, while fault_covered is true vacuously
reason: Proves a fault point existed; the property (fault_covered true and unseen_calls 0) is asserted at lines 730-731.

test_name: a request reader the environment could not hold leaves it unhealthy
broken_impl: the allocation sweep never reaches an allocation, so nothing is checked
reason: Proves populateHandlerAbiTypes allocated at least once. The property is asserted at lines 494-497 for healthy-after-OOM iterations (a poisoning implementation that always reports unhealthy would skip line 497; that gap is in the loop, not this row).

test_name: the ABI alias rows are exactly the aliases the handler ABI registers
broken_impl: no ABI aliases are registered and the table lists none, so equality holds vacuously
reason: Floor on the sweep; the property (published count equals added count, each added alias carries origin abi_alias) is asserted at lines 240 and 247.

test_name: Arena overflow handling
broken_impl: overflow_bytes counts the wrong amount (for example 1) after a 100-byte overflow allocation
reason: allocOverflow adds @sizeOf(OverflowNode) + size to overflow_bytes (arena.zig line 247-262); the test allocates 100 into overflow.

test_name: Arena resetWithAudit returns pre-reset snapshot and zeros state
broken_impl: snapshot.overflow_bytes is wrong (for example 1) for a 1024-byte overflow allocation
reason: Same accounting as line 500: the single overflow allocation is 1024 bytes.

test_name: every in-tree builtin module has a module spec artifact
broken_impl: the spec file holds unrelated or garbage text and the test passes
reason: Each module spec JSON begins with schemaVersion and a specifier field equal to the registry specifier (packages/modules/module-specs/platform/env.json). The spec is rendered from the binding.

test_name: nextGuardId carries INT_PREFIX so the GC cannot mark the slot as a heap pointer
broken_impl: none; line 896 requires id & PREFIX_MASK == INT_PREFIX which is 0xFFFD..., so id cannot be 0
reason: INT_PREFIX is 0xFFFD_0000_0000_0000 (value.zig line 29), so the equality at line 896 already implies id != 0.

test_name: decoder sweep: every bit flip, truncation, and extension
broken_impl: none; failures() at line 2754 forbids an accepted truncation, and every truncation and both extensions must be rejected, so rejected is at least valid.len
reason: truncation_accepted is part of failures(), asserted zero at line 2754, so rejected>0 cannot fail once that line passes.
proposed_assertion: delete the line (or assert rejected >= valid.len)

test_name: decoder sweep: every bit flip, truncation, and extension
broken_impl: decoder rejects every flip, so the leak and over-cap checks never run on an accepted decode
reason: Proves the sweep reached an accepted outcome; the leak, over-cap and typed-error properties over all outcomes are asserted via failures()==0 at line 2754. accepted_unverified is not asserted.

test_name: a Bytes built in a request arena is reclaimed by the arena reset
broken_impl: usedBytes reports 0 or a wrong constant while the arena still contains the object
reason: Establishes bytes were accounted before the reset; the property (usedBytes is 0 after reset) is asserted at line 495, and containment is asserted at lines 489-490.

test_name: simple compile API
broken_impl: compile emits unrelated bytecode (for example a single nop) for the program and the test passes
reason: Top-level programs end with ret_undefined (parser/codegen.zig line 295). Confirm the epilogue opcode before pinning.

test_name: diffContracts upgrades equivalent to equivalent_modulo_laws when dedup fires
broken_impl: none; line 2548 pins the specific law id env.env.pure
reason: found_env_pure at line 2548 pins the law identifier format and content, and is not a weak assertion.

test_name: diffContracts reclassifies when multiple paths match in any order
broken_impl: laws_used holds an unrelated law, or the wrong law for the collapsed /a read, and the test passes
reason: The new side has a redundant env("KEY_A") read, so the law applied is env.env.pure, as in the sibling test at line 2546.

test_name: HandlerProperties.provenSpecNames excludes inverse-polarity facts
broken_impl: provenSpecNames returns an unrelated or single name and the test passes
reason: Defaults make the positive facts true (no_secret_leakage etc., contract_types.zig lines 454-475), and the test already checks the monotonic predicate for no_secret_leakage at line 610.
proposed_assertion: search buf[0..count] for "no_secret_leakage" and expect it found

test_name: attackInput returns a non-empty literal for every property tag
broken_impl: attackInput returns a placeholder such as x for pii_contained or input_validated
reason: The test claims non-emptiness and the switch returns literals, so none for the named claim. Contract-bearing literals are pinned at lines 520-521. Payload text is chosen content with no spec; a golden for the other two would copy the source.

test_name: GC minor collection
broken_impl: none; nursery.used() after two allocations is the precondition for the reset check
reason: Proves the nursery held data before minorGC; the property (used is 0 after the GC, minor_gc_count is 1) is asserted at lines 1564-1565.

test_name: GC allocWithGC triggers collection
broken_impl: GC runs on every allocation (count 3), or twice, and the test passes
reason: Nursery is 256 bytes; two 104-byte aligned allocations fit and the third does not (gc.zig NurseryHeap.alloc aligns to 8), so exactly one minor GC runs.

test_name: every right-hand side is normalized the way the drift gate normalizes the document
broken_impl: an empty rhs passes; scripts/check-grammar-drift.sh compares every rhs with the spec document
reason: Exact rhs text is the spec document, checked by the drift gate. Empty rhs is refused there. A unit-level golden would copy the table.

test_name: cached status text matches canonical lookup
broken_impl: getCachedStatusText returns null for all but one status, or the table is empty
reason: Proves the sweep compared at least one cached text; the property (cached text equals statusTextFor) is asserted at line 1109 for each.

test_name: SDK filesystem reads require canonical allowlist entry
broken_impl: readFileChecked returns truncated or wrong bytes and the test passes
reason: After the allowlist entry the read must return the file contents; the test reads build.zig from the repository root.
proposed_assertion: read build.zig via file_io.readFile and expectEqualStrings(expected, bytes)

test_name: a module signature the environment could not hold leaves it unhealthy
broken_impl: the sweep never reaches an allocation, so nothing is checked
reason: Proves populateModuleTypes allocated at least once; the property (sha256 and env signatures present when healthy) is asserted at lines 493-497, with the same caveat as abi_types.zig:500.

test_name: a large magnitude encodes instead of failing the call
broken_impl: encode writes a wrong string for the denormal (for example 0 or garbage) and the test passes
reason: A denormal 5e-324 must round-trip as JSON number text; parsing the output must give back the same double.

test_name: error formatting
broken_impl: formatFirstError returns text with the wrong line, column or message and the test passes
reason: formatFirstError (error.zig lines 335-358) emits "error at line:col: message"; the test adds the error at 1:9 with message "expected expression".

test_name: trivia offsets index the source they were collected from
broken_impl: a blank_line_run reports blank_lines of 5 or the wrong count and the test passes
reason: The source has two blank runs in order: one empty line after "// header" and two before "const b". Another test pins only a separate case (trivia.zig line 325).
proposed_assertion: collect blank_line_run items in order and expectEqual blank_lines to 1 then 2

test_name: Hybrid runtime reset clears arena allocations
broken_impl: usedBytes reports 0 or a wrong constant while the object is in the arena
reason: Establishes arena use before the reset; the property (usedBytes 0 after rt.reset) is asserted at line 630.

test_name: a guarded call is reachable wherever an expression is
broken_impl: a guarded call in an initializer lowers to several capability_call nodes or an unguarded one and the test passes
reason: The source has one env() call; the sibling case in a return pins count 1 and guarded aux 3 (lines 1020-1021).
proposed_assertion: expectEqual(@as(usize, 1), countTag(in_init.proof, .capability_call)) and expectEqual(@as(u32, 3), guardedAux(in_init.proof).?) after confirming Response.text lowers to no capability_call

test_name: fault violation with counterexample emits JSONL
broken_impl: none; the content checks at lines 542-545 follow
reason: Guards the emptiness of the output; line 542 requires the id fault-uncovered-0, and 543-545 pin method, function and status. None are weak assertions.

test_name: every policy rule resolves through the closed diagnostic catalog
broken_impl: findByCode returns a different catalog entry than the rule's code and the test passes
reason: The test claims the rule resolves through the catalog; the found entry must carry the rule's own code.

test_name: dischargeSpecs implicit default profile gives the narrow Proof remedy
broken_impl: none; saw_remedy is asserted after the loop
reason: Guards the loop; expect(saw_remedy) at line 955 pins the remedy text, and lines 949-952 pin held and unheld names. Not weak assertions.

test_name: contract gate: every failure reason has a distinct stable label
broken_impl: reasonLabel returns a wrong but distinct non-empty label for one reason (for example swapped or renamed), and gate_record.zig:176 serializes it
reason: Nonempty plus pairwise distinct does not pin the stable label. Every arm of reasonLabel (lines 55-66) returns the tag name, so the tag name is the derivation.

test_name: static expert eval summary distinguishes supported and retired asks without model calls
broken_impl: none: the floor only guards an all-unknown corpus, and the next line pins summary.routed
reason: Floor on the count of routed cases; expectEqual(expected_routed, summary.routed) asserts the property (a summary that miscounts fails).

test_name: the routing index never names a tool the model cannot call
broken_impl: none: with checked == 0 the loop checks nothing, so this is the floor of the loop
reason: Floor on non-model tools examined; the property (prompt never names such a tool) is asserted in the loop at line 219-221, whose own floor is this line.

test_name: security probes resolve exactly once and assert their named claim
broken_impl: none: an empty corpus is already refused by validateCorpus on line 432 and by the preceding test
reason: Floor on the corpus; runProbe at line 436 asserts each probe's claim and expectEqual(corpus.len, resolved) pins the count run.

test_name: local client exposes the loop-facing request signature
broken_impl: none: request_fn is a non-optional *const fn (loop.zig:41), so its address cannot be zero
reason: A non-optional function pointer cannot be zero, so the assertion cannot fail.
proposed_assertion: Delete it; the context pointer check on line 1866 is the real claim. Optionally call model_client.request_fn against a fake and assert the result.

test_name: prepared snapshot clamps output to the model capacity left after input
broken_impl: clampOutputToRemainingContext clamps to a wrong value, such as 1 or any number below 8192 but not the capacity left
reason: Test name claims the clamp equals the capacity left. clampOutputToRemainingContext (line 138-155) sets max_output_tokens = context_window_tokens - budget.tokens.total. Capture both before the call, since budget is nulled after.
proposed_assertion: const window = modelLimits(snapshot.config).context_window_tokens; const used = snapshot.budget.?.tokens.total; (before the clamp call) then try testing.expectEqual(@as(u32, @intCast(window - used)), snapshot.config.max_output_tokens);

test_name: reconstructTranscript cleans every allocation failure
broken_impl: none: the sweep succeeding at index 0 means no allocation was exercised
reason: Floor proving the sweep reached at least one induced failure; the property is asserted at line 821 (has_induced_failure), the error set switch, the success-branch checks at 816-818, and leak checking by testing.allocator.

test_name: every skill body is non-empty and every description fits on one line
broken_impl: none: the named claim is non-emptiness itself
reason: Exact skill prose is not contract. Structural and content properties are already pinned per skill by indexOf checks in the later tests (lines 104-120 for fix-violations, route-table, auth-jwt, sql-query and handler-scaffold). canonical-style has no content pin, but body text has no stable golden.

test_name: stand-in hole seeds declare the holes their sources carry
broken_impl: none: a table with no multi-hole seed would still pass the loop, but the two-holes seed is also fetched by id at line 374
reason: Floor that a multi-hole seed exists; per-seed properties (countHoles, expressions, classify) are asserted in the loop at lines 342-352, whose floor is line 339.

test_name: candidateFromSource verifies a guard repair in memory
broken_impl: plan_ids holds a wrong id (not one parsed from plans_json) or a stray one and the test still passes
reason: plan_ids are the ids of the applied plans (lines 497-499 dup plan.id from plans parsed at lines 249-262 out of plans_json). So each id must occur in cand.plans_json, and indexing [0] also pins nonempty.

test_name: ast rewrite: end-to-end ZTS608 → repair_intent → AST primitive → veto passes
broken_impl: none: the loop below requires a replace_arrow_with_function repair, which needs at least one item
reason: expect(saw_arrow) pins the repair intent kind and implies at least one repair; line 763 is not itself weak.

test_name: in-process publisher answers a zttp:sql handler with a result, not a Zig error
broken_impl: execute returns arbitrary non-empty text such as an error string, with no hole frame, and the test still passes
reason: Sibling test at lines 211-216 shows the same hole() handler yields a holes array in llm_text. The sql handler must still return a hole frame, with the projection trimmed, not opaque text.

test_name: search preserves frozen response bytes
broken_impl: none: the response bytes are frozen
reason: The SHA-256 at line 437 and the length at line 435 pin the exact bytes, which fixes the rules count; the loop at 447 asserts ruleMatches for each rule.

test_name: zts_expert_verify_paths schema envelope test (diagnostics ui payload)
broken_impl: none: envelope diagnostics[0] is read at lines 148-149 and items[0].code is compared next
reason: Bounds guard before items[0]; line 157 pins items[0].code equal to the envelope diagnostic code (not itself weak).

test_name: generic clone leaks nothing when an allocation fails partway
broken_impl: none: fail_index == 0 means the clone made no allocation
reason: Floor on the sweep; each failure is asserted to be OutOfMemory at line 1669 and testing.allocator checks leaks at teardown. The loop bound 32 is its own cap.

test_name: production limits are non-zero in every field
broken_impl: none: the named claim is non-zero
reason: Exact production limit values are tuning policy and not contract. A structural check is the assertion itself, and the budget tests at lines 76-88 cover behavior with explicit limits.

test_name: every alphabet member round trips and names itself
broken_impl: name() returns a fixed non-empty string such as "x" for every member and the test still passes
reason: Test name says each member names itself, and name() is defined as @tagName (lines 39-42, 138-141, 165-168, 183-186). The field name is the derivation.

test_name: compile-bench runs one iteration per fixture under 2s
broken_impl: none for the named claim (success and a 2s bound); ir_nodes counts a constant
reason: IR node count is compiler-internal and not a contract; r.success at line 519 is the structural property, and the time bound is asserted at the end. No stable golden exists for the count.

test_name: an all-zero capabilityHash means absent, and a present matrix never produces one
broken_impl: none: the named claim concerns the hash, not len
reason: Floor proving with_caps is non-empty; the claim (hash non-zero and different from the empty matrix) is asserted at lines 170-171.

test_name: a type fault leaves its source line on the runtime for the pool to copy out
broken_impl: the line table resolves the fault to the wrong line (for example line 1 or the function head) and the test still passes
reason: The fault is the call missing() on the third line of the source literal (lines 119-121 in the test), so the resolved line is 3.

test_name: fuzz: parseContentLengthValue is total over arbitrary bytes
broken_impl: none for the named claim (totality); a wrong parsed value would pass but is not the claim
reason: Rejection of empty and whitespace input is already asserted at lines 824-825 and valid values at 817-820. The fuzz branch checks only the shape of accepted input.

test_name: init --extension package fingerprint uses package name checksum
broken_impl: extensionPackageFingerprint yields id 0xffffffff, which Zig rejects, and the test still passes
reason: Zig's manifest fingerprint reserves id 0 and 0xffffffff; the code at line 352 maps into 1..0xfffffffe. The random value itself is not stable, but its range is.
proposed_assertion: const id: u32 = @truncate(fingerprint); try testing.expect(id != 0 and id != 0xffffffff);

test_name: run: a loss of only non-critical proofs is listed and does not fail the gate
broken_impl: none: the next lines require a lost property named deterministic
reason: expect(saw_deterministic) pins the property name and implies at least one lost entry; the loop at 1648-1650 pins severity. Line 1652 is not itself weak.
